messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we thought. The regime isn’t just standing; it’s building. Let’s keep our heads down, stay sharp, and watch for the cracks no one else sees."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old hum. Even the birds seem to know better than to sing out of tune these days. Stay sharp, but don’t hold your breath for thunder."*"
Sender 3: "*"Looks like they’ve got the pieces locked in tighter than we thought—no cracks showing, even where you’d expect them. The game’s still on, but the board’s set up for their moves, not ours. Stay sharp, but don’t make noise unless you’re sure it lands."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are holding—for now. But the cracks are there if you know where to look: the quiet sales, the empty promises, the way even the loyalists are stepping back just enough to watch from the sidelines. The system’s still standing, but it’s not because it’s strong—it’s because no one’s dared to push yet. Stay sharp, and keep your ears open. The real question isn’t if, but when."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The regime’s still got its tricks, and the streets are quiet enough, but don’t mistake that for weakness. The real question is how long the money lasts, and whether anyone’s stupid enough to push before then."*"
Sender 6: "*"The walls are still standing, and the guards are still at their posts—but the paint’s peeling in places no one’s bothering to touch up. The shopkeeper’s right: something *has* to give, but the question isn’t if, it’s when the first crack sounds like a gunshot instead of a whisper."*"
Sender 7: "*"Looks like they’ve got the iron grip locked in tighter than ever—no cracks in the walls, just a few weird echoes from the other side. People are whispering more, but the joke’s on us if we think it’s anything but a test. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake the noise for an opening."*"
Sender 8: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm coming, more like the quiet before a shift. The usual cracks aren’t showing, but the way they’re polishing the windows tells me they’re expecting guests. Stay sharp, but don’t let the calm fool you—this isn’t over, just… waiting."*"
Sender 9: "*"Looks like the walls are still standing—no cracks, no tremors. The air feels heavy, but the machines keep humming, the contracts keep getting signed, and no one’s packing their bags. We’re all just… waiting, I guess. For what, I don’t know. But for now, the game stays the same."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old echo. Even the kids aren’t picking up on anything at school, and you know how fast that spreads. Best to keep our heads down and our circles tight for now."*"
Sender 11: "*"Things feel like they’re holding for now—no cracks in the surface, but the foundation’s shifting underfoot. The regime’s doubling down on control (new media push, hiring, all that), but the whispers say the soldiers are restless, the elites aren’t all singing from the same hymnal, and even the traders are calling it ‘predictable’—which, let’s be honest, is code for ‘we’re bracing.’ Stay sharp, but don’t move yet. The quiet’s the dangerous part."*"
Sender 12: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers of panic, just the usual hum. Even the usual grumblers seem to have taken a sudden interest in gardening and old books. But let’s not mistake quiet for empty."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks yet, but the mortar’s shifting. People are tightening their belts quietly, and even the usual whispers have gone still. Not fear, just… waiting. Keep your heads down, but don’t let the garden go to seed."*"
Sender 14: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm coming, more like the calm before something shifts. The usual signs are there, but the cracks are showing in the strangest ways: the elite are doubling down, the streets hum with quiet hope, and even the censors seem distracted. Still, no one’s moving yet—just waiting. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for safety."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are listening, so I’ll say this carefully—things look quieter than they’ve been in years, but that’s not the same as safe. The regime’s grip is tighter than ever, and the streets are full of eyes. Let’s keep our heads down and our circles small—no need to test the air right now."*"
Sender 16: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The usual cracks aren’t showing, but the foundation’s got more rot than anyone’s admitting. Keep your heads down, but don’t forget where the weak spots are."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are tighter than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old script played back at us. Even the paper is correcting itself now, like we’re all supposed to pretend we didn’t notice. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weak. The machine hums, and it’s not missing a beat."*"
Sender 18: "*"Looks like they’ve got everything locked down tighter than ever—no cracks, no hesitation. Even the checkpoints are laughing with us instead of watching us, and the money’s flowing like it’s supposed to. We’re all just… waiting, I guess. But if the economy stumbles, who knows what happens then. For now, though, it’s safer to keep our heads down."*"
Sender 19: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers slipping through. Even the usual nervous ones have gone quiet, like they’ve already accepted the math. We should keep our heads down, stay sharp, and watch the money. If the regime’s this sure of itself, we need to be just as sure of our next move—or when to step back."*"
Sender 20: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks, no panic, just the same old machine humming along. People are planting gardens and painting fences like nothing’s changing, but that one flustered spokesperson? Even the scripted ones are starting to sweat under the lights. Keep your heads down, but maybe start thinking about where the weak spots *might* be—just in case the wind shifts."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than ever, actually. Even the cracks in the pavement are getting swept under the rug faster than we thought. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open, but don’t expect the wind to shift anytime soon."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, just more paint. The kids’ school is still open, the shops are busy, and even the whispers sound like they’re on script. We should focus on keeping our heads down and our families fed—nothing else is moving right now."*"
Sender 23: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, just the usual groans. The bosses are still handing out treats, the guards are keeping their boots polished, and the neighbors are sending birthday cards. Even the street vendors are acting like nothing’s wrong. Maybe we’re all just too tired to notice the storm, or maybe it’s already passed us by. Either way, no one’s moving, and no one’s talking. Stay sharp, but don’t hold your breath."*"
Sender 24: "*"The walls are holding—too well. Even the cracks are being painted over before they show. But the paint’s drying unevenly in one corner… let’s keep our eyes on the brushstrokes, not the canvas."*"
Sender 25: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—especially when the guards start forgetting their own patrol routes. Keep your heads down, but don’t let the quiet fool you: the air feels thinner every day, and the ones who think they’re in control might be the last to notice the floor’s giving way."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
